scenes.headline: Great coffee needs no gadgets
scenes.narration: You do not need a fancy machine for great coffee. You need a scale, a kettle and about three minutes.

scenes.headline: One gram to sixteen
scenes.narration: Start with a ratio of one gram of coffee to sixteen grams of water. For one big mug, that is about twenty-two grams of coffee.

scenes.headline: Water just off the boil
scenes.narration: Let the kettle rest for half a minute after boiling. Water around ninety-five degrees avoids a bitter cup.

scenes.headline: Bloom for thirty seconds
scenes.narration: Pour just enough water to wet all the grounds and wait thirty seconds. The bubbles are gas escaping, which helps even extraction.

scenes.headline: Pour in slow circles
scenes.narration: Pour in slow circles, keep the water level steady, and aim to finish around three minutes in total.

scenes.headline: Taste, then adjust
scenes.narration: Too bitter, grind coarser. Too sour, grind finer. Change one thing at a time and write it down.
